title: Git vs GitHub in 60 Seconds #shorts
description:
Git and GitHub are not the same thing. Git tracks your code's history on your computer; GitHub hosts it online so your team can collaborate. Commits, branches, merges, push, pull and pull requests, explained visually.

#Git #GitHub #Programming #CodingForBeginners #SoftwareDevelopment #shorts

lines: Git and GitHub are not the same thing.
Here's the difference, in under a minute.
Git is a tool on your computer that tracks every change to your code.
Every time you commit, Git saves a snapshot of your project, with a message and a unique ID.
Branches let you try new ideas in parallel, without breaking the main version.
When it works, you merge it back.
GitHub is a website that hosts your Git repositories online.
You push your commits up to GitHub, and pull your teammates' changes down.
And with pull requests, your team reviews the code before it gets merged.
Git tracks your history. GitHub shares it.
